cpu_temp_high.title: High CPU Temperature
cpu_temp_high.description: The processor is operating above safe temperature thresholds.
steps: Identify and terminate high-CPU processes using the Process Monitor.
Check for dust or obstructions in the physical cooling vents.
Ensure the system is in a well-ventilated area.
If the issue persists, consider reapplying thermal paste or checking fan health.

ram_usage_high.title: High RAM Utilization
ram_usage_high.description: System memory is nearly exhausted, which may cause performance degradation or OOM kills.
steps: Check the Process Monitor for memory-intensive applications.
Restart services that are consuming excessive memory.
Check for memory leaks in custom applications.
Consider adding more physical RAM if this is a frequent occurrence.

disk_usage_high.title: Disk Space Critical
disk_usage_high.description: One or more disk partitions are nearly full.
steps: Run a disk cleanup utility to remove temporary files.
Check /var/log or C:\Windows\Logs for large log files.
Compress or move large, infrequently used files to external storage.
Check for large database files that might need vacuuming.

network_io_spike.title: Unusual Network Activity
network_io_spike.description: A significant spike in network traffic has been detected.
steps: Check the 'Active connections detail' section to identify the source IP/process.
Determine if this is an expected backup or synchronization task.
If unexpected, check for unauthorized data transfers or potential DDoS activity.
Use netstat or tcpdump for deeper inspection if needed.

statistical_anomaly.title: Unexpected Metric Deviation
statistical_anomaly.description: The metric has deviated significantly from its recent historical baseline.
steps: Review the metric graph to see the trend leading up to the anomaly.
Check for recent system changes or deployments that might have caused the shift.
Investigate logs from around the time of the deviation.
Monitor the metric closely to see if it returns to normal or stabilizes at a new level.
